A square is a special type of rectangle whose length and width are equal. For example, consider the square below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144298/assets/a92233299ba67fec2a7712c88afcabeff3973dda07afdd7f91c085c4564e2aa1.png)

We say that the **side length** of this square equals $3\,\textrm{m}.$

Since a square is a special type of rectangle, we find its area by multiplying its length and width. However, since its length and width are equal, we can find its area by *squaring* its side length:

Therefore, the area of the square is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =(3\,\text{m})^{2}\text{ } \\  & =3\,\text{m}\times 3\,\text{m} \\  & =(3\times 3)\times (\text{m}\times \text{m}) \\  & =9\,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
captured.title: Calculating Area

candidates.:tutorial/content:
To calculate the area of a **rectangle**, we multiply its length by its width.

For example, let's calculate the area of the rectangle shown below.

![](images/2f/2f44bfcd63ff10aba31a20082c260c6a1af773e7165b8d8d55db70e5fd0a09f6.png)

For this rectangle, its length is $6\,\textrm{cm}$ and its height is $3\,\textrm{cm}$. Therefore, the area of the rectangle equals

$$
\begin{aligned}
A &= 6cm \cdot 3cm \\
&= (6 \cdot 3) \cdot (cm \cdot cm) \\
&= 18cm^{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

A square is a special type of rectangle whose length and width are equal. For example, consider the square below.

![](images/63/63df4de7035288e9244fc111e546fa71cac312af5ec157075e1931b6835395b7.png)

We say that the **side length** of this square equals $3\,\textrm{m}$.

Since a square is a special type of rectangle, we find its area by multiplying its length and width. However, since its length and width are equal, we can find its area by *squaring* its side length:

Therefore, the area of the square is

$$
\begin{aligned}
A &= (3m)^{2} \\
&= 3m \cdot 3m \\
&= (3 \cdot 3) \cdot (m \cdot m) \\
&= 9m^{2}
\end{aligned}
$$
